summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -2 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates −; dollar 0; brl 0; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Coffee +14.3%; weakest: KC wheat -14.4%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.13% (+17 bp in a month), 2-year 4.81% (+5 bp); 2s10s curve +32 bp (+12 bp in a month). Rising long yields raise carry and funding costs and pull money out of commodities. A steepening curve led by the long end often reflects inflation or term-premium worries; T-bill yield 4.01% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.56 (+1.0% in a month, +3.3% YTD). USD/BRL 5.044 (-1.1% in a month): little changed. USD/CNY 6.664 (-0.5%); USD/MXN 18.70 (+8.2%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -1.4% in a month (+11.9% YTD); VIX 19.1. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 99.32 $/bbl (+12.9% in a month), Brent 112.40, ULSD 4.691 $/gal (+3.1%), natural gas 2.82 (-9.6%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -6.1% in a month, Shanghai Composite -7.4%, Hang Seng -8.6%, yuan +0.5% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 14 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (42%); S&P GSCI +1.9% in a month; gold -7.2%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
